details:
I'm working on a tool that helps people install dependencies, and right now they have to:

- asset imported, get some message about dependencies 

- click "add X to VCC" button 

- agree in VCC

- return to project

- be confused because dep is still not there (problem)

- come back to VCC and figure out how to install recently added package into specific project (problem)

- hopefully done and dependency installed

Proposal: 

- have a vcc:// endpoint that would not just request adding project to VCC but will request importing it into currently open project. User will have to click "add to VCC" and then "import into project X" would be sequentially shown. If it exists in VCC - skip the add to VCC screen and prompt directly to import it to active project. 

This way user controls everything and there is no need to do fragile workarounds for the sake of ease of use

Then flow turns into:

- asset imported, get some message about dependencies 

- click "install X via VCC" in unity editor

- (only if not added already) click "add X to VCC" in VCC popup

- click "import X to this project Y"

- done, dependency marked as installed

Known issues/blockers: 

- URLs don't let VCC know which exact project sent them which will be a problem

Right now its only achievable via manually editing a manifest file, as far as i understand, which is a no go for me personally - too fragile and too big of a potential for damage

This is potentially useful for lots of projects with heavy use of dependencies/custom shaders/etc. that still try to be user friendly on import. Not essential by any means, but it would improve new users ability to use prefabs/packages and it doesn't seem to have been proposed yet:3
title: Add ability to request import of a VPM package from the editor
